newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MARK DOMINATES BUDAPEST CURRENCY FUTURES MARKET.
newsitem.headline: MARK DOMINATES BUDAPEST CURRENCY FUTURES MARKET.

text.p: The mark dominated trade on Budapest's currency futures market, accounting for almost half the Budapest Commodity Exchange's (BCE) turnover and all of the Budapest Stock Exchange's (BSE) trade.
Most BCE trade in the German unit, which accounted for 9,690 of the total 19,223 lots traded, was for September, which fell 0.11 to 112.50, and December, which fell 0.25 to 116.96 forints.

The mark saw massive block trades in all its delivery dates except for the most distant March 1998, which remained untraded, although a late bid raised its price 0.60 to 120.10 forints while all other months fell.
Yen and Swiss franc contracts seemed to have temporarily lost their appeal with the subdued mood on both sections failing to show any distinctive trend in rates.
BSE trade was unusually high at 1.22 million forints, with 1.09 million of that taken up by March mark deals.
